newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends mid-range, falls with U.N./Iraq new.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends mid-range, falls with U.N./Iraq new.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed slightly lower on Wednesday in the middle of the session's trading range, having drifted around a 50 cents range in thin volume, brokers said.
Jan Brent closed 2 cents down at $22.72 a barrel.
The contract touched an intra-day high of $23.02 but eased back to a low of $22.56 when the U.N. reported that arrangements for Iraqi oil sales were in place.
Brent retraced some of the losses shortly before the close.
"Strength in (NYMEX) heating oil produced a little short covering in the last five minutes," said one broker.
The U.N. Security Council sanctions committee on Iraq formally approved the December pricing formula for pending sales of Iraqi crude under the U.N. oil-for-food deal, diplomats said on Wednesday.

Iraq announced at the OPEC meeting in Vienna, which kicked off on Wednesday, that it could resume oil exports "within a matter of weeks" and that it expected to export between 700,000 and 800,000 barrels per day.

OPEC sources said they expect the current production quota of 25.03 million barrels per day, which takes into account Iraqi exports, to be rolled over into 1997. But there was debate over whether this would be for six months or a year.
IPE Dec gas oil closed earlier at the day's low of $216.25 a tonne, 75 cents down on the day.
